title: Action-log round-trip test compares only 2 of 6 command kinds; the #partial switch silently skips everything else
detail: Other kinds match nothing, so no comparison runs — the test passes even if the codec corrupts them. The fixture only produces Draw_Pipe/Set_Pipe_Priority, leaving 4 of 6 ODN-11 codec branches untested.
recommended_fix: Compare all six command kinds (or fail on an unmatched kind), and build a log containing Upgrade/Demolish/Lane_Weights/Junction_Triage entries so the whole binary codec round-trips.

title: Severance-reroute test claims to prove mid-edge packets survive, but the assertion cannot distinguish them from post-demolish spawns
evidence:
+	// E1 branch 1: with an alternative, SOME of the mid-edge packets must
+	// survive the reroute (deliveries continue beyond fresh spawns' share)
+	del_after := state.flow.sla[streaming].delivered
+	if del_after <= del_before { tfail(t, "reroute must keep deliveries flowing") }
+	_ = sev_drops_before
detail: del_after > del_before also holds when every delivered packet was spawned after the demolish — zero mid-edge survivors still passes. The captured sev_drops_before (which could isolate the claim) is immediately discarded via `_ =`.
recommended_fix: Stop demand before demolishing (or compare drops against on_pipe_count) so continued delivery can only come from rerouted mid-edge packets; use sev_drops_before in the assertion.

title: Grace-reset test passes even with the instant re-arm exploit it claims to pin
detail: 100 healthy ticks refill the 200-tick window gradually (+5/tick after the streak gate), but an instant full re-arm on the first healthy tick (the never-lose exploit) reaches the same value. The assertion cannot distinguish them.
recommended_fix: Assert intermediate state: after one healthy tick grace must have refilled by at most grace_refill_per_tick, not jumped to full.

title: Pool-exhaustion test comment says 'narrow leg' but the code wires the wide boot network
evidence:
+	// no pipes: every spawn unroutable... need in-flight accumulation instead:
+	// wire one leg so packets pile without delivering (narrow leg, huge demand)
+	testkit_wire_boot(state, 0)
detail: The comment describes wiring one narrow leg; the code calls testkit_wire_boot, which draws parallel wide pipes plus wide legs and sets a priority dial. Neither the narrow leg nor 'one leg' exists in the executed path.
recommended_fix: Fix the comment to describe testkit_wire_boot's wide topology, or actually draw a single narrow leg so the fixture matches the stated setup.

title: flow_fixture's header says the spine is the only contended link; its body comment says the contention point is the legs
evidence:
+// bare topology: host --standard--> router --legs--> h1,h2 — every terminal
+// routable, the spine the only contended link (15 u/s standard).
---
+	// The contention point is the LEGS (email flows house->router->house; the
+	// spine carries only streaming) — the dial goes on the legs.
detail: Two contradictory statements of where contention lives, in the same proc. One of them misdescribes the fixture; a reader cannot tell which link the QoS assertions actually exercise. The header's '15 u/s standard' also breaks when tier_name='wide' is passed.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the header to match the body (legs are the contention point, dial on legs) and drop the tier-specific capacity claim from the generic fixture comment.

title: Tests hardcode class indices (u16(0), u16(1), sla[0], priority=1) while looking them up via class_index elsewhere
evidence:
+	streaming := u16(1) // catalog order: email, streaming
+	email := u16(0)
+	n_e := neutral.flow.sla[0] // email is class 0 in the catalog
detail: Class identity is pinned by raw literal in several tests, yet flood_plan and other tests resolve it with class_index. A catalog reorder silently repurposes these fixtures (priority=1 dials the wrong class) instead of failing loudly.
recommended_fix: Resolve email/streaming via class_index everywhere and assert the lookup succeeded; delete the literal-index shortcuts.

title: Assertions bake shipped-catalog tunables (drain cap 2, exit 93, costs 234/360) into magic numbers
evidence:
+	if state.health.meter_pct != bal.meter_start_pct - 2 {
+		tfailf(t, "drain: got %d, want %d", state.health.meter_pct, bal.meter_start_pct - 2)
---
+	expected := start_grace - 20
detail: Tests read bal for some values yet hardcode the consequences of others (drain 2, flap burn 20, delta 234, draw 360). Any balance retune breaks them even when the behavior under test remains correct.
recommended_fix: Compute expectations from bal (e.g. min(severity/10, meter_drain_per_tick_max), tier cost_per_tile values) instead of restating catalog numbers as literals.

title: Severance tests hardcode pipe id 2 after the fixture discards the Edit_Result containing the real id
evidence:
+	nb, direct, _ := topology_apply_edit(&state.topology,
+		Command{kind = Cmd_Draw_Pipe{a = router, b = h1, tier = std}}, cat, state.budget, 1)
+	state.budget = nb
---
+	_ = direct
---
+	direct := u32(2)
detail: The fixture receives the drawn pipe's id in Edit_Result and throws it away (`_ = direct`); both tests then hardcode u32(2) on the assumption ids start at 1 and increment per draw. Any id-scheme change silently targets the wrong pipe.
recommended_fix: Return the Edit_Result's pipe id from severance_fixture and use it, instead of re-deriving the id from a literal.

title: submit_c swallows validation errors — fixture draws can silently no-op
detail: On validation failure the command is silently dropped (no tfail, no return). Fixtures using submit_c (severance alt path, boot wiring, lane weights) can end up with a different topology than the test assumes, failing later at confusing assertions.
recommended_fix: Take the testing.T handle and tfailf on any error, or return bool/Edit_Error so callers must acknowledge a rejected fixture edit.

title: test_rng_streams_independent tests the opposite: same seed reproduces the identical stream
detail: The name promises stream independence; the body seeds two generators identically and asserts equal outputs. No independence property is exercised anywhere — the name misdescribes the test.
recommended_fix: Rename to test_rng_same_seed_reproduces, or add the actual independence check (different seeds/stream selectors must diverge).

title: Autowire junction tier list {wide, wide} retries the identical command — a deterministic no-op second attempt
detail: For junctions both tier entries are wide, so a failed first submit is retried with the byte-identical command against unchanged state — it cannot succeed. The retry-escalation shape only makes sense for houses ({standard, wide}).
recommended_fix: Use a single-element tier list for junctions (or a real fallback tier), so the loop retries only when the retry can differ.

title: test_port_limits computes then discards two tier lookups (_ = basic, _ = std)
evidence:
+	basic, _ := tier_index(cat, "standard")
+	_ = basic
---
+	std, _ := tier_index(cat, "standard")
+	wide, _ := tier_index(cat, "wide")
+	_ = std
detail: Two 'standard' tier indices are fetched and immediately discarded (one confusingly named 'basic'); the test actually draws with 'wide'. Dead lookups left behind — the variable named basic holding the standard tier compounds the confusion.
recommended_fix: Delete the unused basic/std lookups and keep only the wide tier actually used by the test.

title: test_batch_validate_all_then_apply names the standard-tier variable 'wide'
detail: The variable called wide holds the index of the 'standard' tier and is then used for the batch draws. Same-file sibling tests bind wide to tier_index(cat, "wide") — the same identifier means two different tiers within one test file.
recommended_fix: Rename the variable to standard (or fetch the wide tier) so identifiers match the tier they hold.

title: Growth test promises near-junction validation but asserts only min separation — over all nodes including non-growth boot nodes
evidence:
+	// E31: growth positions are seeded-deterministic and every spawn respects
+	// min separation + near-junction growth (outward from the router mesh).
---
+			if manhattan(ta.node_pos[i], ta.node_pos[j]) < bal.growth_min_dist_tiles {
+				tfailf(t, "nodes %d and %d violate min separation", ta.node_id[i], ta.node_id[j])
detail: The comment claims both min-separation and near-junction checks; only separation is asserted, and the all-pairs sweep also judges hand-placed boot nodes that growth never positioned — a catalog min_dist exceeding the boot spacing fails the test for unrelated reasons.
recommended_fix: Track which nodes growth spawned and assert both invariants (min separation and within growth_spawn_near_junction of a junction) on exactly those, not on all pairs.

title: 'header-only log must reject' truncates to 8 bytes — at most magic+version, not a complete header
detail: The same test reads header.seed/era/catalog_hash/logic_hz afterwards, none of which fit in 8 bytes — so bytes[:8] is a truncated header, not a 'header-only, zero commands' log. The case the comment names (valid header, no records) is never tested.
recommended_fix: Relabel the case as a truncated header, and add the actual header-only case: a log_write output from a state with an empty action_log.

title: test_severance_reroute_or_drop builds the pressure plan once at tick 0 and reuses it for ticks 1..60
detail: plan.tick stays 0 for all 60 steps, so no set piece can ever enter plan.set_pieces (activation is evaluated against plan.tick) — the test's traffic model silently excludes the surge timeline the planner exists to produce.
recommended_fix: Re-plan per tick (scripted_plan_pressure(cat, tick, ...)) inside both loops, matching how the real step loop uses the Director.

title: tlogf logs by recording a passing expectation
detail: Every tlogf call inflates the suite's passed-expectation count by design, so pass counts no longer reflect assertions. The comment admits the channel abuse.
recommended_fix: Use the testing package's actual log facility (or plain fmt output) instead of a synthetic passing expectation.

title: Autowire can never wire a spawned node that is neither a junction nor Residential
evidence:
+			if pass == 0 && !is_j { continue }
+			if pass == 1 && (is_j || t.node_role[i] != .Residential) { continue }
detail: Pass 0 wires junctions, pass 1 wires Residential terminals; any other grown role (e.g. a second content host from growth_roles) matches neither pass and stays unwired forever, retried every tick. The autopilot silently strands such nodes.
recommended_fix: Handle all terminal roles in pass 1 (or assert growth_roles contains only junction/residential types) so grown nodes are always wireable.
